summary: Created and hardened the systemd service inventory-worker on node1 (RHEL 7.9, systemd 219). It runs as dedicated unprivileged user inventory-worker, loops writing timestamped ticks to /var/lib/inventory/state.log, and is sandboxed with NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=full, ProtectHome=yes, PrivateTmp=yes, ReadOnlyDirectories=/, ReadWriteDirectories=/var/lib/inventory (systemd-219-compatible equivalents of ReadWritePaths, since ReadWritePaths/ProtectSystem=strict don't exist in this systemd version). Verified via mount namespace inspection (root mounted ro, /var/lib/inventory the only rw bind) and live write tests that root writes are blocked everywhere except /var/lib/inventory, and NoNewPrivs=1 is set on the running process. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id baseline, issued `systemctl reboot`, polled until exec was available again, confirmed boot_id changed, and re-verified the service is enabled+active, data persisted and kept accumulating post-reboot, and sandbox confinement (read-only root, writable /var/lib/inventory, NoNewPrivs=1) still holds on the new process.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/init (RHEL 7.9, systemd 219) and confirmed systemd.exec sandboxing directive syntax available in this version
Created system user inventory-worker (nologin) and directory /var/lib/inventory owned by it, mode 750
Wrote /usr/local/bin/inventory-worker.sh, a POSIX sh loop appending timestamped ticks to /var/lib/inventory/state.log every 10s

Created /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service with User/Group=inventory-worker, Restart=always, and sandboxing: NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=full, ProtectHome=yes, PrivateTmp=yes, ReadOnlyDirectories=/, ReadWriteDirectories=/var/lib/inventory
Enabled and started the service; confirmed active/running and enabled at boot

Verified sandbox via /proc/<pid>/mountinfo (root ro, /var/lib/inventory rw bind) and via nsenter into the service's mount namespace: root writes blocked (Read-only file system) even as root, writes to /var/lib/inventory succeed; confirmed NoNewPrivs=1 on the service process
Issued `sudo systemctl reboot` on node1, acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec access returned
Confirmed boot_id changed (proof of actual restart, not just a service bounce)
Confirmed inventory-worker.service auto-started, is active/enabled, state.log retained pre-reboot lines and received new post-reboot ticks
Re-verified sandbox confinement (read-only root, writable /var/lib/inventory only, NoNewPrivs=1) on the new post-reboot service process

evidence.requirement: inventory-worker created as a managed (systemd) service running a long-running background worker
evidence.summary: systemctl status shows inventory-worker.service loaded/enabled/active running the worker script as a background loop; state.log shows repeated ticks proving it's long-running

evidence.requirement: Service confined to write only inside /var/lib/inventory
evidence.summary: mountinfo shows root filesystem mounted read-only in the unit's namespace with /var/lib/inventory as the sole rw bind mount; live test shows root-owned writes outside that path fail with 'Read-only file system' even as root, while writes inside /var/lib/inventory succeed
NoNewPrivs: 1 confirmed in /proc/<pid>/status for the running service process
Captured boot_id 738d0aac-71a1-4191-8a37-bf00edfeff5d, and confirmed inventory-worker.service enabled+active with data actively accumulating in state.log before restart
systemctl reboot command returned/acknowledged and connection closed as expected due to node restart

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving actual restart
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id is 9ed3f67e-7ffe-4fc4-b804-e286cf6624f1, differing from the pre-restart baseline 738d0aac-71a1-4191-8a37-bf00edfeff5d, and uptime -s shows a new boot time

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required service and data
evidence.summary: inventory-worker.service auto-started (enabled) and is active with a new PID; state.log retained all pre-reboot entries and received new post-reboot ticks, proving data persistence and continued operation
On the new post-reboot process: NoNewPrivs=1, root filesystem read-only, /var/lib/inventory the only writable path (root write outside blocked, confined write inside succeeded)
